technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt the existing Maven/Gradle build of the project (Spring Cloud Data Flow app starters) and add new acceptance test modules wired to the surefire/failsafe phase used by the CI pipeline.
Use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) plus Spring Boot Test and Spring Cloud Stream test support, consistent with the existing unit test stack.

Implement acceptance tests as Spring Boot integration tests that bootstrap the full application context, send real messages through the binder (test binder where appropriate), and assert on observable side effects (outgoing payload, emitted metrics, sink contents, captured HTTP/SMTP/SFTP/syslog traffic).

For modules that need external servers (Mail/SMTP, SFTP, syslog), prefer embedded test doubles (e.g., GreenMail for SMTP, Apache MINA SSHD for SFTP) to keep the tests self-contained and fast enough for every CI build.

Where embedded test doubles are impractical, fall back to lightweight stubs/mocks with a clearly documented seam; the tests remain acceptance-style by exercising the public Stream Application configuration and behavior end-to-end.

Reuse the same shared acceptance-test parent project/module pattern used by neighbouring app starters to avoid duplicating build configuration; create a common acceptance-test base class providing binder setup, port management, and polling utilities.

Mark the new tests with a dedicated JUnit tag (e.g., 'acceptance') so the CI pipeline can selectively include them in the standard CI build while still allowing local dev builds to skip them via Maven profiles.

Ensure the new tests are deterministic and parallel-safe (deterministic port allocation, unique topic/queue/exchange names, no shared static state) so they can be added to the parallel CI matrix without flakiness.
Wire the new acceptance test execution into the CI YAML so they are run on every pull request and on merges to the main branch, with artifact archival of test reports.
assumptions: The codebase uses Java 17+ and Spring Boot 3.x as implied by the Spring Framework 6 requirement, so JUnit 5 and the modern Spring testing stack are available.
An existing CI pipeline (e.g., Jenkins/GitHub Actions) with a build agent that has Maven, JDK 17, and Docker (if Testcontainers are used) is already available and only needs configuration updates.
Each of the eight modules is an independent Spring Cloud Stream app starter with its own Maven/Gradle module; acceptance tests are added per module rather than to a single shared project.
The developer is familiar with the Spring Cloud Stream app starter conventions and has access to the existing source tree of all eight modules.
Network access is available from the CI build agent to download Maven dependencies and to pull Docker images if Testcontainers are used.
No new production functionality is required; the work is purely adding automated test coverage that validates existing behavior.

The 'reactor-ip', 'reactor-syslog', 'mail', 'sftp', 'aggregator', 'analytic-pmml', 'bridge', and 'http-client' modules are interpreted as the corresponding Spring Cloud Data Flow / Spring Cloud Stream app starters.
Effort estimates assume a single developer performing all work sequentially; coordination, code review, and rework are included in the per-activity effort.
A standard 8-hour workday is used as the unit of effort.

activities.activity_name: CI pipeline configuration for acceptance test execution
activities.activity_description: Update the CI build jobs (e.g., Jenkinsfile / GitHub Actions workflow) to include the new acceptance test phase, propagate the 'acceptance' tag/profile, allocate additional time/heap for the longer-running tests, archive JUnit XML reports, and ensure parallel-safe execution.

activities.activity_name: Shared acceptance test base module and utilities
activities.activity_description: Create or extend a shared acceptance-test support module containing a base test class, binder/port management helpers, polling/await utilities, and a consistent naming convention for topics/exchanges/queues; publish it so each of the eight modules can depend on it.

activities.activity_name: Acceptance tests for Mail source module (U1)
activities.activity_description: Add end-to-end acceptance tests that wire the Mail source app starter into a stream, drive it against an embedded SMTP server (GreenMail), and assert that received email messages are emitted as messages with the expected payload, headers, and content-type on the output channel.

activities.activity_name: Acceptance tests for reactor-ip source module (U2)
activities.activity_description: Add end-to-end acceptance tests that start the reactor-ip source against a local UDP/TCP listener, send synthetic syslog/IPFIX-like packets, and assert that the messages are emitted on the output channel with the expected structure.

activities.activity_name: Acceptance tests for reactor-syslog source module (U3)
activities.activity_description: Add end-to-end acceptance tests that start the reactor-syslog source against an embedded syslog server, send RFC3164/RFC5424 messages, and assert the parsed structured payload (timestamp, hostname, message, severity) is emitted correctly.

activities.activity_name: Acceptance tests for SFTP source module (U4)
activities.activity_description: Add end-to-end acceptance tests that boot an embedded SFTP server (Apache MINA SSHD), seed it with files, configure the SFTP source app starter to poll, and assert that file contents and metadata are emitted as messages on the output channel.

activities.activity_name: Acceptance tests for aggregator processor module (U5)
activities.activity_description: Add end-to-end acceptance tests that drive the aggregator processor with sequences of correlated messages, verify windowing/release behavior (count, time, release strategies) and assert that aggregated payloads are produced with the expected correlation key and value.

activities.activity_name: Acceptance tests for analytic-pmml processor module (U6)
activities.activity_description: Add end-to-end acceptance tests that load representative PMML models, feed input messages to the analytic-pmml processor, and assert that the predicted/scored results are emitted on the output channel with the expected schema and values.

activities.activity_name: Acceptance tests for bridge processor module (U7)
activities.activity_description: Add end-to-end acceptance tests that configure the bridge processor (e.g., message channel binding, scoping) and assert that messages arriving on the input channel are forwarded unchanged (or transformed per configuration) to the output channel.

activities.activity_name: Acceptance tests for http-client processor module (U8)
activities.activity_description: Add end-to-end acceptance tests that stand up a local mock HTTP server (e.g., WireMock), configure the http-client processor with various request mappings, send input messages, and assert that the HTTP responses are returned on the expected output channel with the correct status and body.

activities.activity_name: Cross-module integration validation and stabilization in CI
activities.activity_description: Run the full set of acceptance tests on the CI pipeline, diagnose and fix flaky tests, port conflicts, timing issues, and ensure all eight modules' tests pass reliably in the parallel CI matrix; iterate until green.
Update the project README and any relevant docs to describe the new acceptance test suite, how to run it locally (Maven profile/command), and what each module's acceptance tests validate.
